question: Should Gateway socket.drain preserve existing slow-subscriber compatibility or intentionally close slow WebSocket clients during session teardown?
rationale: The PR's central value is reliable teardown delivery, but the current implementation reaches existing session-event subscribers and changes slow-consumer behavior from drop to disconnect without an explicit accepted contract.

options.title: Preserve compatibility by default
options.body: Use the existing drop-if-slow behavior for current subscribers unless a narrower, documented strict drain path is approved.

options.title: Approve fail-closed drains
options.body: Keep close-on-slow teardown delivery, but document and test the disconnect behavior as an intentional Gateway contract.

options.title: Split the contract
options.body: Land message-subscriber routing separately and track a dedicated Gateway design for guaranteed teardown delivery under backpressure.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility by default
recommendation.body: Use the existing drop-if-slow behavior for current subscribers unless a narrower, documented strict drain path is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest available history across Gateway runtime broadcast behavior and public protocol documentation.
